proposals: ACER should publish a single annual table of entry and exit gas tariffs at every EU cross-border interconnection point, on a comparable €/MWh basis, since no such table exists and that absence is part of why the tariff stack on landlocked buyers is under-discussed.

ENTSOG should publish monthly gas transit and import volumes by member state and interconnection point on a consistent basis, so that the collapse in Slovak and Austrian throughput — Eustream below 10% of historical levels — can be tabulated rather than only described.

The European Commission should publish, before the 30 September 2027 pipeline-gas deadline, an assessment of who bears the rising transmission costs for Austria, Czechia, Hungary and Slovakia, with options for sharing them, answering the question the phase-out regulation left open.

The European Commission should report the inland pipeline capacity and tariff cost of moving gas from under-used coastal terminals such as Krk and Ravenna to the landlocked states, since terminals ran at about 52% utilisation and the bottleneck this piece finds is in the pipes, not on the coast.

Eurostat should correct and complete the 2025 annual gas balances for Hungary, Slovakia and other members currently returning implausible values, so that consumption for the year the phase-out began can be analysed on official data rather than 2024 figures.
